complete_examples.text: Therefore, large wheel-rail local contact stresses are formed and produce significant damages on wheel/rail materials in the forms of wear, rolling contact fatigue, rail corrugation, and material plastic deformation, etc.

The goal of constructing more accurate and robust wheel-rail contact models is to predict the wheel/rail rolling contact fatigue [13] and wear [14], the development of rail defects [15], and local strain/stress distribution [16], and especially important, to evaluate the running safety and dynamic behavior of train-structure systems [17,18].
